scoreMeaning: Out of10 for the current unpublished profile’s purposeful silence, static legibility and restraint. Strong current application with minor controllable repetition; excludes sound quality, motion quality, tested return-visit comfort, audience recognition and the unbuilt website.

strengths.finding: Silence is complete rather than missing polish.
strengths.evidence: README.md uses theme-selected PNGs and ordinary text/links; no authored media playback or mascot interaction is present. The visible profile communicates without waiting for an action or requiring an audio cue.

strengths.finding: Meaning survives small-scale character detail loss.
strengths.evidence: At320px, the native name, handle, bio, Hey I’m Nag heading and project descriptions remain the information carriers. The small header moth adds identity, while no instruction depends on its mitten, eye direction or color alone.

strengths.finding: The visual identity is recognizable as a coherent proposal across the two themes without making a human-recognition claim.
strengths.evidence: 1440px and320px previews retain the same avatar silhouette and heyNag wordmark. The universal day avatar stays distinct in dark GitHub chrome; the header paint changes appropriately.

strengths.finding: The project list remains quiet and direct.
strengths.evidence: Actual scrolled320px captures show three native linked names with concise factual descriptions and no badge wall, animation loop or image-only product explanation. The private-work sentence frames the public sample without disclosing private material.

strengths.finding: Future continuity preserves a useful hierarchy.
strengths.evidence: continuity.json keeps Nag as author, the moth as companion, native static GitHub assets, useful work visible without mascot interaction and no link to the unbuilt website.

deductions.finding: The bio and README opening repeat software/systems, useful tools, curiosity and caring how software feels. On a320px visit these similar introductions are read in separate stacked regions before reaching the public work. It is warm but slightly redundant for a returning reader.
deductions.confidence: medium-high as a textual/rendered observation; no measured return-visit frustration
deductions.improvementCriterion: Compare a shorter README opening that adds one distinct personal detail or moves sooner to the public work, while preserving the private-work context and plain tone. Evaluate the actual320px scrolled result before changing it. Do not attribute GitHub-owned navigation/achievements height to the draft.

recommendations: Keep the proposed GitHub profile static and silent. Do not add a GIF, soundtrack, fake Play control or sensory flourish to demonstrate the mascot system.
Keep native project names/descriptions as the meaningful content and the image alt text as a short identity description; do not attempt to explain tiny gestures through audio.
Consider tightening only the repeated bio/README introduction in a later copy pass; current wording is acceptable for this local proposal.
When implementing heyNag.com, make silent default, intentional finite replay and optional sound consent explicit. The current no-forced-sound contract is a direction, not tested behavior.

continuityAssessment.decision: Support the current GitHub application and the written continuity direction, with distinct evidence status.
continuityAssessment.demonstratedNow: Static common avatar/header identity, consistent personal naming and useful project text in local GitHub DOM previews.
continuityAssessment.plannedNotBuilt: Website investigation/share action, interruption, static/reduced-motion story and project narrative navigation.
continuityAssessment.futureRefinement: Specify silent-by-default behavior and separate reversible opt-in if sound is ever commissioned. Avoid autonomous repeated attention demands during reading. Require new implementation review rather than treating this contract or prior mascot approval as website approval.
continuityAssessment.claimBoundary: Immediate recognition in continuity.json is a design goal; no unfamiliar-viewer recognition, authorship attribution or memory result is demonstrated.
